title: Release packages: cargo xtask dist writes the deb, AppImage, MSI, DMG, server archives and SHA256SUMS.txt
spec: Add an xtask crate (workspace member, publish = false) and a cargo alias so that `cargo xtask dist --version <v> --out <dir> [--target linux-x86_64|windows-x86_64]` builds crewcraft and crewcraft-server in release mode and writes, named <app>-<version>-<os>-<arch>.<ext>: the client .deb (an ar archive of debian-binary 2.0, control.tar.gz with control and md5sums, and data.tar.gz installing /usr/bin/crewcraft 0755, a desktop entry, the SVG and PNG icons in the hicolor theme and the license files; Depends read from the ELF libraries and symbol versions the binary links, failing on an unmapped library; plus the OpenGL, keyboard and Wayland-or-X11 libraries the window loads at run time, with the rest of both display stacks as Recommends), the client .AppImage (the pinned AppImage type2 runtime 20251108, passed in with --appimage-runtime or CREWCRAFT_APPIMAGE_RUNTIME and refused unless its SHA-256 matches, followed by a zstd SquashFS image from mksquashfs of an AppDir holding AppRun, crewcraft.desktop, crewcraft.png, .DirIcon and the .deb's files under usr/; the AppDir also carries the runtime's MIT license (assets/appimage/RUNTIME-LICENSE.txt), the LGPL 2.1 text for its libfuse code copied from /usr/share/common-licenses/LGPL-2.1, and a SOURCE.txt naming the runtime's release, source tag and how to replace it, in usr/share/licenses/appimage-runtime/; --no-appimage leaves it out), the Linux server .tar.gz and Windows server .zip (one top folder named like the asset holding the binary, the license files and a README on first-run and serve), the client .msi (per-machine install into Program Files\CrewCraft, Start menu shortcut, Add/Remove Programs entry with the icon, ProductName CrewCraft, Manufacturer CrewCraft contributors, the fixed UpgradeCode {7B22B52D-5053-41BB-A254-FF039F9B37C3}, a ProductCode per version, a major upgrade that removes strictly older versions and refuses when a newer one is installed, files in an embedded MSZIP cabinet), and SHA256SUMS.txt in sha256sum format over every asset in the folder. On macOS only, --target macos-universal builds x86_64-apple-darwin and aarch64-apple-darwin, checks each is the right Mach-O architecture, joins them with lipo -create, and writes crewcraft-<v>-macos-universal.dmg (hdiutil create -format UDZO, volume CrewCraft, holding CrewCraft.app and an Applications link; the app has Contents/MacOS/crewcraft, an Info.plist with CFBundleIdentifier io.github.setsuad.crewcraft, CFBundleName CrewCraft, CFBundleShortVersionString the release version, CFBundleVersion the MSI version numbers, LSMinimumSystemVersion 11.0, NSHighResolutionCapable true and CFBundleIconFile crewcraft.icns, Contents/Resources/crewcraft.icns with PNG entries from 16 to 1024 px, PkgInfo and the license files) and crewcraft-server-<v>-macos-universal.tar.gz; elsewhere it fails before building. The plist, icns and bundle layout are pure functions tested on Linux. Without --target, dist builds linux-x86_64 and windows-x86_64, or macos-universal on a Mac. Versions are MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -alpha.N, -beta.N or -rc.N; Debian writes the pre-release with ~ and the MSI version is MAJOR.MINOR.(PATCH*1000 + 100+N alpha, 200+N beta, 300+N rc, 900 release). Archives are reproducible: sorted entries, parent folders first, root owner, one fixed time from SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH or the commit. Windows binaries are cross-compiled for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and must import no MinGW runtime DLL. All Rust except the MinGW-w64 linker, mksquashfs, the AppImage runtime and Apple's lipo and hdiutil (docs/NON-RUST-DEPENDENCIES.md). The desktop entry carries StartupWMClass=crewcraft and the window sets the app id crewcraft (apps/crewcraft/src/main.rs, one line).
